text:
ben: heads-up — our nightly client-side benchmark shows a 18% p50 regression on text-gen for the 8k model. repro harness attached, but numbers differ a lot between replay vs synthetic.
maya: can you paste the harness commands? are you reusing connections or opening new ones per req? :thinking:
ben: synthetic: `wrk` with keepalive on, 64 connections, persistent. replay: our replay-harness opens a new HTTP/1.1 connection per session (to match real traffic). Command excerpts:
ben: ```
# synthetic
wrk -t12 -c64 -d120s --latency http://redwood-inference/v1/generate

# replay (our tool)
python3 replay.py --sessions sessions.json --open-per-request
```
oliver: big flag: open-per-request will add TLS handshake + TCP 3-way for every request — that'll blow up median and tails if the server isn't warmed. Also Nagle can add small delays for tiny initial packets. Try TCP_NODELAY and connection reuse for apples-to-apples.
sara: another big skew: KV cache warmup. Replay opens fresh sessions targeting many users => KV caches miss and cause extra compute on early tokens. Synthetic uses repeated same prompt, so cache hits. That explains lower synthetic latency.
ben: interesting — profiler snapshot shows extra kernel selection chatter during first tokens: multiple kernel launches and fallback paths. snippet from nvprof:
ben: ```
=== kernel-switch log ===
kernel_select: quant_fwd (inlined)
kernel_select: fallback_slow_gemm
launch_time: +12ms
launch_time: +9ms
```
maya: that suggests model variant selection/conv path triggers on sequence length or KV state. Might be the runtime trying different tiling/kernels on first requests. Did anything change in the auto-kernel-picker recently?
ben: rolled back a tiny allocator change yesterday — but perf correlates more with client-side connection pattern. When I replayed with persistent connections and pre-warm priming requests (100 short prompts) numbers matched synthetic.
oliver: TL;DR troubleshooting checklist I use:
- Match connection pattern (keepalive / conn-per-request)
- Match protocol (gRPC vs HTTP/1.1/HTTP2)
- Match payload sizes and inter-arrival times
- Warm KV cache: run priming set
- Ensure socket opts: TCP_NODELAY, disable Nagle for small chat packets
- Profile kernel switch counts + kernel binary selection at startup

perf-bot: Alert: nightly-ci/bench: p50-textgen-8k +18% vs baseline (1991110000). Investigation ticket: INF-4821
sara: on gRPC vs REST: gRPC multiplexes streams so fewer TLS handshakes but can amplify head-of-line effects on long tails if one stream stalls. For our workload, gRPC reduced handshake overhead but increased occasional stalls when batching heuristics coalesced large batches.
maya: for apples-to-apples, I'd recommend a bench matrix: replay vs synthetic, conn reuse vs conn-per-request, gRPC vs HTTP2 vs HTTP/1.1, with KV primed vs unprimed. small matrix but captures major axes.
ben: final quick win: set TCP keepalive and TCP_NODELAY on clients, pre-warm KV cache for 5% of sessions, and run one run with connection reuse — that cut our observed p50 back within 2% of baseline. I'll open a PR to update the replay harness default to reuse connections for infra perf runs, and add a separate churn test to mimic client churn.
maya: sweet. please add the exact commands and the priming script to the ticket so SRE/bench can rerun.
ben: will do, attaching gists to INF-4821. Thanks all :thumbsup:
